description: ipld/cid_util.rs does u32::try_from(header_bytes.len()).expect("header_bytes length must fit in u32"). On 64-bit targets usize is 64-bit and headers will never exceed 4 GiB, so this is practically infallible. But on 32-bit targets (usize == u32), this is always fine too since usize == u32. The assert is correct but the expect message is misleading. More importantly, if headers ever exceed 4 GiB (a theoretical future concern), the process panics instead of returning an error. Consider returning Result<Cid, CidError> or using a debug_assert with a saturate fallback.
title: core: cid_for_article uses .expect() for u32::try_from(header_bytes.len()); infallible on 64-bit targets but silent footgun on 32-bit
